Rising costs and import restrictions have exacerbated the situation since the export ban from China in 2020. While laboratories have sought alternatives from Cambodia, ethical concerns about animal sourcing have emerged. A startup, backed by Joe Lonsdale, plans to establish a breeding facility to alleviate supply constraints.

items.summary: Mumbai faces severe air pollution challenges, primarily driven by rapid urbanization and industrial growth that extends beyond city limits. Since 2011, vehicle registrations have nearly tripled, while pollution sources include dust, industries, and waste burning. A comprehensive regional clean air plan is essential to address these issues effectively across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region. Efforts must include improved monitoring, cleaner energy sources for industries, and sustainable transport solutions.

items.title: Gov't to add 9 types of behavior to legal definition of stalking
items.title_zh: 政府不应在跟踪的法律定义中添加9种行为
items.summary: The government is pushing to expand the definition of stalking to include tracking victims' locations and monitoring their social media activity, among other actions, as part of efforts to swiftly separate perpetrators from victims, the justice ministry said Tuesday. The ministry said an amendment to the Act on Punishment of Crime of Stalking was proposed Oct. 26 to make nine types of controlling behavior within a relationship criminal offenses. The nine types of behavior are forcing victims to maintain a relationship, tracking their whereabouts, notifying them that they are being monitored, exercising digital control over them, interfering with their social relationships, controlling their access to or use of private information, creating threats or instilling fear, threatening their pets and isolating them from others. Under current law, these acts are not recognized as distinct forms of stalking, limiting law enforcement's ability to intervene unless they involve physical assault or bodily injury. items.title: Drug ring busted for making meth with cold medicine
items.title_zh: 毒品戒指因用感冒药制成冰毒而被捣毁
items.summary: Police said Tuesday they have busted a criminal ring suspected of manufacturing billions of won worth of methamphetamine using cold medicine. The group allegedly bought large quantities of cold medicine to extract pseudoephedrine, a chemical used to illegally make methamphetamine, and produced 1.36 kilograms of the drug between April 2025 and June this year, according to the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency. The amount is estimated to be worth 4.2 billion won ($3.1 million) and can be taken simultaneously by 40,000 people. Police have referred 13 suspects involved in the scheme, including the group's five members, to the prosecution on drug-related charges. The group had used an abandoned apartment to begin producing the drug in April last year before investigators were tipped off about the scheme in December. Police began apprehending the suspects in June after an undercover investigation. Investigators found that a traditional Korean medicine pharmacist and five other suspects helped the group manufacture the drugs. items.title: NIS asks 2,100 public institutions to conduct emergency cybersecurity checks
items.title_zh: NIS要求2100家公共机构进行紧急网络安全检查
items.summary: Korea's spy agency has asked 2,100 public institutions to conduct emergency cybersecurity inspections following a series of cyberattacks on financial firms that resulted in customer data breaches, government sources said Tuesday. The National Intelligence Service (NIS) has called on the central government agencies and local governments to carry out their own security checks based on a checklist, the sources said. Separately, the NIS plans to conduct its own vulnerability assessments of critical information and communications infrastructure in the public sector under its jurisdiction, the sources said. The assessments are expected to be completed by mid-November. Local financial institutions, including banks, savings banks and insurance companies, were hit by a series of cyberattacks last month, exposing about 100,000 cases of personal information across the industry, including email addresses, names and phone numbers. The Dynamic of the Congolese Elite in Korea, known in French as Dynamique de l'Élite Congolaise en Corée du Sud, held an extraordinary and elective general assembly, bringing together members of the Congolese academic and professional community. The meeting opened under the leadership of Eloi Fataki, vice president of the General Assembly, followed by a presentation by professor Merlec Mpyana, who reviewed the organization's history and its mission to unite and empower Congolese intellectuals and professionals in Korea. Reagan Ingoma, the outgoing president of the Executive Bureau, presented the organization's 2025-2026 activity report, outlining achievements, challenges and key developments during his tenure. items.title: Kwangwoon University sets sights on becoming AI, robotics powerhouse
items.title_zh: 光旺大学着眼于成为人工智能、机器人强国
items.summary: Kwangwoon University unveiled plans to establish itself as a leading institution in artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics by nurturing talent and expanding access to education in the two fields as the era of physical AI takes shape. The university held a ceremony on Thursday to unveil its AI and robotics education strategy, drawing some 400 attendees, including lawmakers, local government officials, university presidents, education and research representatives, students and local residents. The event also aimed to strengthen partnerships ahead of the 2027 World Robofest Championship, an international youth robotics competition the university is set to host next year. "We aim to nurture talent who will drive advances in robotics worldwide and build a future where robots serve people," Kwangwoon University President Yoon Do-young said. The event featured congratulatory remarks from former National Assembly Speaker Woo Won-shik, Reps. items.title: Korea launches 3,600-ton submarine, boosting naval deterrence, defense export capacity
items.title_zh: 韩国发射3600吨级潜艇，提升海军威慑力和国防出口能力
items.summary: Korea’s Navy and Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA) launched the Seo Hui (SS-088), the nation’s second 3,600-ton Dosan Ahn Changho-class Batch-II diesel-electric attack submarine, during a ceremony at Hanwha Ocean’s Geoje Okpo Shipyard on Tuesday. The vessel is named after Seo Hui (942–998), a prominent diplomat and statesman of the Goryeo Dynasty renowned for using strategic negotiation to fend off a massive invasion by the Khitan-led Liao Empire in 993, securing vital territory along the northwestern border without shedding blood. Navigating regional security threats around the peninsula, Korea designated his name to symbolize military foresight, national crisis resolution and maritime sovereignty defense. The ceremony was attended by around 200 officials, including National Assembly Speaker Cho Jeong-sik. Following naval tradition, Cho’s wife, Cho Mi-seon, cut the launching ribbon attached to the vessel, symbolizing new life breathed into the newly built warship, followed by a ceremonial champagne bottle break against the hull. items.title: Kookmin University professor recognized among World's Top 2% Scientists
items.title_zh: 国民大学教授跻身世界前2%科学家行列
items.summary: Kim Dae-hwan, a professor at Kookmin University’s School of Electrical Engineering, has been included in the 2026 World’s Top 2% Scientists list compiled by Stanford University and Elsevier. The list recognizes the top 2 percent of researchers in their respective fields based on a comprehensive analysis of research impact, including citation metrics and publication output, drawing on data from Elsevier’s Scopus database. Kookmin University said Kim has focused on the physical characterization of semiconductor devices based on indium gallium zinc oxide, a material used in next-generation memory and display technologies. He has published 484 papers in international journals and major academic conferences proceedings, garnering 7,926 citations, according to Scopus data as of October. “I am honored to be recognized among the World’s Top 2% of Scientists, and I owe this achievement to the faculty members and students, research collaborators and industry partners who have worked alongside me,” Kim said. items.title: Lee, first lady to get new passports after personal data exposure
items.title_zh: 李，第一夫人在个人数据泄露后获得新护照
items.summary: The foreign ministry said Tuesday it is taking steps to reissue passports for all 168 people affected by an online leak of sensitive personal information, including President Lee Jae Myung and first lady Kim Hea Kyung, as police investigate how the data was exposed. “The foreign ministry is swiftly taking measures to ensure the smooth reissuance of passports for all affected individuals, including the president and first lady,” ministry spokesperson Park Doo-soon said during a briefing. Police have opened a preliminary investigation into the leak, which involved personal information belonging to the presidential couple, Cabinet members, senior officials from Cheong Wa Dae and the foreign ministry, security personnel and reporters traveling with the presidential delegation. The National Police Agency launched the investigation after passenger information and sensitive personal data related to the presidential aircraft were found posted online. items.title: Police release identity of suspect in Seoul building arson
items.title_zh: 警方释放首尔大楼纵火案嫌疑人的身份
items.summary: Police on Tuesday released the identity and mug shots of a suspect accused of setting fires at two patent firms in southern Seoul last month and leaving 26 people injured. The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency posted the photos of Lee Myung-soo, 77, on its website following a decision by a review committee. Lee is suspected of committing arson in two buildings in Seoul's southern ward of Gangnam on Oct. 20, He was taken into custody shortly after the fires and was referred to the prosecution last week on charges of arson and attempted murder. Investigators believe the suspect planned the arson and was likely aware of people inside the offices. Lee has claimed that he was scammed by the patent firms and only wanted to scare people, not hurt them. Korea releases the identities and mug shots of those suspected of committing serious crimes when there is substantial evidence that they committed the offenses.

items.title: Consumer prices up 2.8% in October, remain in 2% range for 2nd month
items.title_zh: 10月份消费者价格上涨2.8% ，第二个月保持在2%区间
items.summary: Korea's consumer prices rose 2.8 percent in October from a year earlier, data showed Tuesday, as agricultural product prices continued to decline despite energy costs remaining elevated. According to data from the Ministry of Data and Statistics, consumer price growth eased to 2.8 percent in October from 2.9 percent in September and 3.1 percent in August. The data ministry said petroleum products' prices advanced 14.9 percent year-on-year in October, contributing 0.56 percentage point to the month's year-on-year inflation rate. It was the sharpest growth since 15.5 percent posted in July. In detail, diesel prices jumped 19.7 percent year-on-year in October, while gasoline prices increased a sharp 11.6 percent. Korea relies heavily on imports to meet its energy needs. The report showed that prices of industrial products overall rose 4.4 percent year-on-year in October due to higher global energy prices, with those of mobile phones and computers climbing 10.8 percent and 26.2 percent, respectively. Prices of imported automobiles, on the other hand, fell 3.9 percent over the same period. In ad

items.title: Saudi, French and Greek defense ministers discuss defense cooperation in phone call
items.title_zh: 沙特、法国和希腊国防部长在电话中讨论国防合作
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Minister of Defense Prince Khalid bin Salman held a phone call with French Minister of the Armed Forces and Veterans Affairs Catherine Vautrin on Monday. During the call, the ministers reviewed Saudi-French strategic defense relations and ways to strengthen them. They also discussed regional and international developments and the coordination of efforts regarding them to enhance security and stability in the region and the world. Also on Monday, Prince Khalid bin Salman held a phone call with Greek Minister of National Defense Nikos Dendias. During the call, they reviewed ways to strengthen current and future defense cooperation between the two countries. They discussed joint efforts to enhance regional and international security and stability in light of current developments in the region.

items.title: King Salman, Crown Prince congratulate Iotova on winning Bulgarian presidential election

items.summary: RIYADH — Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman and Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman congratulated Iliana Iotova on her victory in the presidential election of Bulgaria. In separate cables sent to Iotova, the King and the Crown Prince expressed their sincere congratulations and best wishes for her success and for the Bulgarian people’s continued progress and prosperity.

items.title: GCC launches anti-dumping investigation into paper imports from India, China, and Thailand
items.title_zh: 海湾合作委员会对从印度、中国和泰国进口的纸张展开反倾销调查
items.summary: RIYADH — The General Secretariat of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) announced that the Permanent Committee on Anti-Harmful Practices in International Trade has decided to open an anti-dumping investigation into imports into GCC states of uncoated writing, printing, and graphic paper in rolls or rectangular (including square) sheets, originating in or exported from India, China, and Thailand.The committee’s decision follows a preliminary report by the Technical Secretariat of Anti-Harmful Practices in International Trade, which operates under the GCC General Secretariat. The initiation notice, with full details of the product under investigation and the procedures, was published in the technical secretariat’s official bulletin, Issue No. 59, dated November 2, 2026, which is available on the GCC General Secretariat’s website.Director General of the Technical Secretariat Mahfoudh Al-Raqadi said the measures are being taken under the GCC Common Law on Anti-Dumping, Countervailing Measures and Safeguards and its executive regulations, and the World Trade Organization’s Anti-Dumping Agreement. He added that announcing the investigation gives all interested parties the opportunity to defend their interests at every stage.

items.title: Jordan Crown Prince condemns Houthi attacks during meeting with Saudi Crown Prince
items.title_zh: 约旦王储在会见沙特王储时谴责胡塞武装袭击
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman received Jordanian Crown Prince Al Hussein ibn Abdullah in Riyadh on Monday.At the outset of their meeting, the Jordanian Crown Prince conveyed the greetings of King Abdullah of Jordan to Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman and the Crown Prince, who, in turn, conveyed the greetings of King Salman and his own greetings to King Abdullah.Prince Al Hussein condemned the terrorist Houthi militia's attacks on Saudi Arabia and affirmed Jordan's full solidarity with the Kingdom against any threats to its security and the safety of its citizens and residents, and its full support for the measures Saudi Arabia takes to protect its assets and resources.The leaders also reviewed the historical relations between the two countries and their peoples, as well as their shared commitment to expanding cooperation across all fields.The meeting was attended by Deputy Emir of Riyadh Prince Mohammed bin Abdulrahman, Minister of Foreign Affairs Prince Faisal bin Farhan, and Minister of State and Cabinet Member Khalid Al-Issa.From the Jordanian side, the meeting was attended by Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates Ayman Safadi, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Maj. Gen. Majdi Al-Harasis, and Director of the Crown Prince's Office Dr. Zaid Baqain.

items.title: India reaffirms solidarity with Saudi Arabia, condemns Houthi attacks
items.title_zh: 印度重申声援沙特阿拉伯，谴责胡塞武装袭击
items.summary: JEDDAH — Indian Ambassador to Saudi Arabia Vipul has reaffirmed India's unwavering solidarity with Saudi Arabia amid the exceptionally difficult circumstances prevailing in the region, strongly condemning the Houthi attacks targeting civilian and energy infrastructure in the Kingdom and expressing hope for the swift restoration of peace and normalcy. “India stands in complete solidarity with our Saudi brothers and sisters during the very difficult situations prevailing in the region. We condemn in the strongest manner the attacks which are taking place on civilian and energy infrastructure in the Kingdom. We hope peace and normalcy will soon return to the region,” he said while speaking to Okaz/Saudi Gazette during his visit to the headquarters of Okaz Organization for Press and Publication in Jeddah on Sunday. The ambassador was received by Editor-in-Chief of Okaz newspaper and General Supervisor of Saudi Gazette Jameel Altheyabi and Director General of Okaz Organization Abdullah Al-Hassoun.The meeting between Vipul and Altheyabi focused on further consolidating the strategic partnership between the two nations. The ambassador emphasized that Saudi-Indian relations are anchored in a long and distinguished history of friendship and close ties between the two countries and their peoples.“What is most important in relations between India and Arabia is the people-to-people connection that began several centuries ago and now serves as the foundation of relations between the two countries. These historic ties continue to flourish under the leadership of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Saudi Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman,” he said. Vipul underscored the significance of the recent exchange of visits between the leadership of the two countries, highlighting their pivotal role in deepening bilateral relations and further consolidating the strategic partnership. He also expressed his commitment to building on these longstanding ties and expanding avenues of cooperation in ways that advance the shared interests of both nations. “Our focus is now on promoting trade and investment. We have a wonderful and extensive energy relationship, which will continue to grow further in the years to come. We are also working together to expand cooperation in technology, culture, and education, with a strong focus on sustainability. Given the large young populations in both India and KSA, we see enormous opportunities and possibilities,” he said. The ambassador expressed hope that India and Saudi Arabia would continue to demonstrate new pathways for the world through their growing partnership. “We also work not only bilaterally but also in the G20 and other multilateral organizations,” he said, highlighting the importance of cooperation on international platforms alongside their expanding bilateral engagement. Vipul also commended Okaz and Saudi Gazette for their keen interest in covering developments in India and their role in showcasing the diverse dimensions of India-Saudi relations. He expressed his eagerness to maintain and strengthen engagement and cooperation with both publications. During the visit, the ambassador was shown archival coverage of India published in both newspapers. The delegation was also briefed on a presentation tracing the history and evolution of Saudi-Indian relations and toured a pavilion displaying historical photographs and articles published by Okaz newspaper, reflecting its extensive coverage of bilateral ties over the decades. Vipul was accompanied by Consul General of India Fahad Ahmed Khan Suri; Consul of Commerce & Press, Information & Culture Mohammed Shabeer K; and other officials. The meeting was also attended by Deputy Editor-in-Chief of Okaz Abdullah Obaian; Assistant Editor-in-Chief Khalid Al-Jarallah; Managing Editor of Saudi Gazette Anas Alyusuf; and several other officials and editors from the two newspapers.

items.title: Economic Council reviews price stability amid intensifying global pressures
items.title_zh: 在全球压力加剧的情况下，经济委员会审查价格稳定情况
items.summary: RIYADH — A meeting of the Council of Economic and Development Affairs (CEDA), held via video conference on Monday, reviewed the Ministry of Economy and Planning’s monthly report on global economic growth and its outlook amid rapidly shifting geopolitical dynamics. The report highlighted the Kingdom’s pivotal role in strengthening the resilience of the global economy and supporting international price stability by ensuring the continuity of energy supplies and providing alternative export routes. These efforts have helped soften the impact of geopolitical changes on global markets, underscoring the Kingdom’s standing as a reliable partner and its active role in global economic stability. The report also examined the implications for the Saudi economy, noting that economic indicators show a capacity for price stability despite mounting global pressures. It attributed this resilience to effective economic and structural policies that have contained inflationary pressures and protected purchasing power. The Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) reached 55.3 points, its highest level since February 2016, reflecting growing business confidence and the Saudi economy’s adaptability as it continues to diversify under Saudi Vision 2030. The council discussed the Ministry of Health’s presentation on progress in the health transformation plan, the transfer of health clusters to the Health Holding Company, and the national health insurance scheme. Ten health clusters are transferring to the Health Holding Company, with steps set out to complete the transfer of the remaining clusters by early 2027. The aim is to separate the provision of health services from their regulation and financing: the ministry will regulate and supervise the sector, while the Health Holding Company will deliver services through 20 health clusters in line with the Saudi Model of Care. The presentation also highlighted the clusters’ achievements in improving access to care and its quality. To monitor government entities’ progress on their assigned tasks, the council reviewed a report by the Project Management Office of the CEDA Secretariat on the implementation of its decisions and recommendations in the third quarter of 2026. The report detailed the council’s outputs at the central government level and within the represented entities, with comprehensive completion statistics. It noted an increase in the number of entities scoring above 98% on performance indicators and a decline in outstanding or delayed tasks. The council also considered several procedural matters, including a progress report on directives to develop the startup and venture capital sector; a report on the activities of the National Program to Combat Commercial Concealment; the monthly executive summaries of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) and the Wholesale Price Index (WPI); the quarterly executive summary of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) report; the monthly executive summary on foreign trade; and the underlying reports. The council issued the necessary decisions and recommendations.

items.title: HR Ministry sets January 31 deadline for private firms for mandatory disclosure of training data
items.title_zh: 人力资源部为私营公司设定1月31日强制披露培训数据的截止日期
items.summary: RIYADH — The Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development has urged private sector establishments employing 50 or more workers to disclose their training data through the Qiwa platform before the January 31, 2027 deadline. The ministry stressed that disclosure is mandatory for all establishments covered by the decision, irrespective of whether they have implemented training programs for their employees or not. The ministry clarified that establishments that have implemented training programs must disclose the number of trainees, the programs conducted, the number of training hours, and the associated costs. Establishments that have not implemented any training programs are also required to disclose this fact. However, such disclosure does not exempt them from fulfilling their legally mandated training obligations.The ministry revealed that the proportion of private sector establishments disclosing their training data exceeded 53 percent in 2025, compared with more than 38 percent in 2024. This progress reflects ongoing efforts to establish a unified national database that will contribute to the development of training policies and enhance workforce efficiency. The ministry indicated that the disclosed data had helped support several initiatives, most notably cooperative training, which benefited more than 120,000 students by the end of 2025. The data also contributed to the decision requiring covered establishments to train graduates and job seekers at a rate of two percent of their total workforce. The ministry emphasized that disclosing training data is intended to promote investment in skills development, align training programs with labor market needs, and enhance workforce productivity and preparedness, thereby advancing the objectives of Saudi Vision 2030.

items.title: 6-month jail, SR100,000 fine for assisting residency and labor law violators
items.title_zh: 6个月监禁，因协助居住和劳动法违规者而处以10万斯洛伐克里亚尔的罚款
items.summary: RIYADH — The Ministry of Interior has affirmed that anyone who transports, employs, shelters, or provides any form of assistance to individuals violating residency or labor laws faces a maximum fine of SR100,000, imprisonment for up to six months, and deportation for expatriates. The ministry urged the public to report violations of residency, labor, or border security laws by calling 911 in the regions of Makkah, Madinah, Riyadh, and the Eastern Province or 999 in all other regions of Saudi Arabia.

items.title: Saudi, Jordanian FMs discuss regional developments in phone call
items.title_zh: 沙特、约旦FM讨论地区电话发展
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Minister of Foreign Affairs Prince Faisal bin Farhan received on Monday a phone call from Jordanian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates Ayman Safadi. During the call, they discussed the latest regional developments and the importance of continuing coordination and consultations in this regard.

items.title: Saudi Crown Prince sends message to Chinese president
items.title_zh: 沙特王储向中国国家主席致电
items.summary: BEIJING — Saudi Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman has sent a message to Chinese President Xi Jinping. The message was pertaining to bilateral relations between the two countries and the ways to further develop them. It also dealt with issues of common interest. Minister of State, Member of the Cabinet, and National Security Advisor Dr. Musaed Al-Aiban delivered the message to Minister of Foreign Affairs Wang Yi, who is also member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and director of the Office of the Central Commission for Foreign Affairs, during their meeting in Beijing on Monday. **media[2788750]**
